newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - March 20.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - March 20.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Thursday:
* On Wednesday, the Dow Jones shed 18.88 points to 6,877.68. PLDT's ADR dipped $1 1/2 to $57 1/2.
* The peso closed higher 26.333 from 26.336 to the dollar.
* The Philippine Stock Exchange composite index fell 15.03 points to 3,200.61.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was unchanged at 10.03125 percent.

* The Supreme Court virtually rules as illegal all efforts to amend the Constitution to extend the term limits of President Fidel Ramos and other officials when it declared yesterday that there was no enabling law on initiatives to change the Charter. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

* The country's balance of payments in the first two months of 1997 yielded a surplus of $463.8 million, down by 40 percent from the BOP surplus of $769.2 million posted in the same period in 1996. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

* Newspaper BusinessWorld reported that economists say the Central Bank's aggressive bid to boost its foreign exchange reserves by actively buying dollars in the market could only hurt the country's trade balance even more.
* Food and beverage firm RFM Corp said it took in four business groups as minority partners in its thrift bank unit, the Consumer Savings Bank.

* The Business Daily said, quoting brokerage houses that internal problems hounding the Philippine bourse are making foreign fund managers apprehensive about the capability of the stock exchange to operate professionally.
* Manila Times and the Inquirer say a battle for corporate control is brewing at A. Soriano Corp (Anscor), the holding company of the Soriano family's diverse commercial and financial interests.
* Manila Bulletin said Lepanto Consolidated Mining Co, one of the country's biggest gold producers, announced the completion of its Victoria gold project in the northern province of Benguet.
* Bulletin reported that the Manila Electric Co's (Meralco) board declared a 30 percent stock dividend to stockholders on record May 16, 1997.
